Concepts-and-terms/Comfort-Heroes-and-Ma.title: Comfort Heroes and Mastery Depth
Concepts-and-terms/Comfort-Heroes-and-Ma.content:
A comfort hero isn’t just a hero you’ve played a lot — it’s a hero where your mental model has depth across multiple axes: how you build it, which talents you take, who you fight, and what the team actually needs from you.
That depth tends to accumulate in layers:
No knowledge — you’re pattern-matching from watching others. You know Treant is a support, probably. You hit things.
Broad understanding — you know the kit’s shape. Treant roots, Treant heals. You contribute something real, but your decisions are reactive.
Knowledge — you know the specifics that change decision-making. Leech Seed’s orb flag, the cooldown breakpoints, when a talent changes the ability’s role entirely. This is where itemisation starts becoming intentional rather than mimicry.
Reasoning — you understand the interactions between game concepts. Roots prevent mobility but are always purgeable, so every root Treant applies is also a signal to the enemy that dispel has value. That changes how you think about their item timing and your own window of effectiveness.
Intuition — you’ve internalized the reasoning so thoroughly it no longer requires conscious processing. You feel the game state through the hero. You know before the fight starts that this particular lineup punishes your root duration, so you shift your positioning and timing without articulating why.

These levels run across four axes: itemisation, skill selection, hero matchups, and role in the game. But there’s a fifth axis that underlies all of them — the hero’s base attributes.
Movement speed, base armor, attack animation, attack range, base damage, stat gains per level. These aren’t flavour — they’re the physical grammar of the hero. Treant’s high base HP and mediocre movement speed shape when you can walk up to apply a root and when you can’t. His attack animation is slow enough that auto-attacking in a fight is a conscious choice, not a reflex. His strength gain means his early-to-mid power curve is steep, which affects when you can play aggressively without items. A player who hasn’t internalized these attributes will make subtly wrong decisions constantly — overcommitting to trades they can’t win, undervaluing positions where their base stats actually dominate. Mastery of attributes is quiet but it separates players who understand the hero from players who understand the abilities.

The other thing worth noting is that intuition isn’t the end of learning — it’s the beginning of a wider one.
When you’ve internalized a hero deeply enough that your own decisions stop costing mental load, you free up cognition to look outward. You stop thinking about what Treant does and start thinking about what the enemy Witch Doctor is about to do, whether their carry’s attack animation lets them contest this creep wave, whether the offlaner’s movement speed means they can reach the rune before you. Intuition on your own hero is what creates the headspace to reason about everyone else.
This is also how comfort heroes become templates. Once you have intuition on Treant, learning a hero with similar physical constraints — slow, tanky, short-range — transfers faster. And when you face a new matchup, you’re not starting from scratch: you’re applying the same reasoning structures you built on a hero you already understand from the inside out.

Concepts-and-terms/Pool.title: Pool
Concepts-and-terms/Pool.content:
Concept of Pool is to have limited 3 heroes per role. Typically they are strong heroes that are generally regarded to be suited to the role.
Limiting the pool has the benefit of increasing your overall mastery. See Comfort Heroes and Mastery Depth
Heroes in pool should fill a Role and ideally all fit into the same style, in order to ease playing similarly between matches.
There can be flavor of the month builds but they should not be included in the pool as they are unlikely to be good for extended periods. Goal is to gain mastery in limited amount of heroes and expand there.
Example of a pool for solo ranked grinding would be:

Treant Protector
Lich
Crystal Maiden

Despite the heroes being very different they offer somewhat similar capabilities as all are:

Strong laners
Counter initiation/save
Not item dependant

Concepts-and-terms/Questions.title: Questions
Concepts-and-terms/Questions.content:
Description
Goal of this practice is to force yourself to ask questions and spend a bit of tie to come up with solutions on the spot. This is in attempt to get out of the habit of having clear cut autopilot mode.
Questions
What do I need to do in this match?
Using a Treant Protector example you can identify that opponents Troll Warlord, is their wincon and when he pops ulti+bkb, you need to be there to overgrowth him to waste both of them.
Often times the “task” itself can be extremely simple and it can come in two phases as well:
“As a Crystal Maiden my job is to not have my high impact ult be cancelled, so it can do a lot of damage in middle of teamfight”
In order to accomplish that you need:

Ability to move to the teamfight >

Force
Blink Dagger


Ultimate not to be cancelled

Keeping track of enemy disables and waiting
Having a BKB



What prevents me from doing my task?
There can be various obstacles preventing you from being effective in the match
Opponent can run away

Atos
Orchid
Opponent is going to rightclick you to death
Force
Ghost Scepter
Eul
Glimmer
Opponent is going to stunlock you
BKB
Opponent is going to out sustain
Spirit vessel
Crozier

What objective are we playing for?
Identify the strongest core on your team and play around them, optimally they will inform you where you are playing or what objective you are playing around.
What can I do right now?
Things are usually moving in a direction and you should determine if you have time to do some useful things right now

Warding
Stacking
Hitting creeps

Who is our win condition?
Usually either Pos1 or Pos2
What kills them? Can you help?
If the enemy silence or disarm is killing your Win condition, can you build items to dispel?
If the opponent has a short window of opportunity, can you kite / delay them?
What is enemy’s win condition?
Usually but not often their Pos1. Goal is to identify that can you help kill them and if so how? If you cannot or should not kill the, how can you prevent them from performing.
What team absolutely needs?
This could be an Spirit vessel in a match where there is huskar, which you need to identify and build if no one else is doing it.

Quickly

Heroes/Crystal-Maiden.title: Crystal Maiden
Heroes/Crystal-Maiden.content:
Tips
Crystal nova
Value of the rank 1 nova is in the ability to hit to targets at once. 110 magic damage x 2 for 115 mana is really big value, but it is not that urgent post laning.
Also provides vision so you should always check Pillars for wards by barely having the sentry range on the pillar and then casting nova to see if there is a ward. This way your sentries can cover a lot more ground and accidentally catch observers elsewhere too.
Decoy
Decoy can be cast while channeling ult and it Disjoint projectiles. So a Vengeful Spirit stun could be avoided by a nicely placed decoy
Decoy is also a potent farming tool as you’ll be maxing the W first and by the time you have Shard you should be able to pull two camps together > Create decoy and destroy it with crystal nova to apply frostbite on all of the targets, which will kill all of them except ancients.
Itemization
There is surprising amount of flexibility and need to consider your itemization, as you really only need Tranquil Boots and Shard and everything else exists to fill very specific purpose.

Heroes/Nightstalker.title: Nightstalker
Heroes/Nightstalker.content:
Tips
Void
Shard upgrades the radius and damage isn’t actually lower during the day, meaning the spell is a really good farming tool all throughout the game. During day you might not have the mana regen to spam it constantly so be aware of that
Crippling fear
Aura effect, which means escaping it can be tricky. Consider how the opponents can avoid it and see if your build can adjust. For example Eul and Force are both dispelled if you cast Nullifier on the target.
Activate before blinking on backline casters, particularly if they have mobility spells.
Midnight Feast
HP on hit is active even during day, giving you a surprising amount of sustain and ability to git creeps at full hp
During night use freely if any of the following applies:

Not at full HP
Not at full mana
Killing a camp and it is sped up by eating a creep

Dark Ascension
Grants flying and flying vision and instant nighttime for a period. Best used during a daytime at the start of a teamfight as it will give your team insane visibility and allow you to pick your targets.
Can be used during the night if the flying vision is deemed worth it.
When this is on CD you are fairly useless during the day, so use when the enemy is committed to the fight. If they can just walk away it can easily be wasted.
Day / Night
During night you should put pressure on opponent as you are way stronger, during day you need to take the foot of the pedal and farm.

Heroes/Shadow-Shaman.title: Shadow Shaman
Heroes/Shadow-Shaman.content:
Tips
Ether shock
Underwhelming spell, but eventually will become your way of Waveclear. You can opt to take 1 point in laning in order to secure ranged creep.
Hex
Instant cast disable with break from talents. If vision permits you can cast this on opponents Magnus from way back and you’ll start walking towards them. In the case they blink in the cast range the spell is fired off and the followup spells are prevented.
Note that break is only useful against defensive passives, as the enemy cannot hit anything while hexed anyway.
Shackles
Similar laning utility as Bane’s brainsap as it does ok damage, but it also heals your for the same amount. Great value if your lane buddy also puts in a couple of hits.
Mass Serpent Wards
If you want to take a T1 by yourself you can actually put sentry on the tower range, which takes the aggro and holds it for 10 hits. Pop wards right after and the wards have a lot more time to churn down the HP.
Heroes can be trapped between the wards and it can be really good if done properly, but horrible if your carry is trapped there with no ability to even kill the wards.

Heroes/Treant-Protector.title: Treant Protector
Heroes/Treant-Protector.content:
Skills
Q - Nature’s grasp
During laning, the one value point is used to finish kills or let your core run away from kill attempts. More than that cannot be sustained earlier and you are spending already mana to spam living armor.
Later Waveclear safely from Invisibility where your teammates cannot go. This is why it is maxed second.
Nature’s grasp is also perfectly sized for taking double camps around the map if you really need to farm that blink or get to level 6.


                  
                  Counts as trees 
                  
                

Nature’s grasp can be used to extend your nature’s guide passive even if opponent is going away from the treeline.
For example, you might want to push a wave, but the creeps are positioned awkwardly. You can then walk to the middle of the lane, and as long as the passive doesn’t expire before the vines are in place you don’t lose the invisibility.


W - Leech seed
Extremely good value point, as it is free and allows you to get an extra autoattack afterwards. As a support, it is not worthwhile to max, as after laning ends you have hard time utilizing it.
As a support you can put it on autocast immediately, as you are less concerned “wasting” it on creeps as you would as a core.
E - Living armor
Awesome skill that you’ll be maxing first and putting on your Pos1 & Pos2. Note that the healing is great for the manacost, but the biggest value is the damage block. If you can put this on any hero as they are being focused at any point of the game, you’ll be getting insane value out of the mana cost.
Usually, Pos5 cannot venture to far objectives without Pos1 losing his cool, however Treant can keep him topped up with living armor and mitigate the tilt.
After laning, this skill shouldn’t really be of CD, as long as there are towers that can be healed. Instruct team to defend towers, as even at 1% they can be healed quite quickly.


                  
                  Building healing in perspective 
                  
                

With level 10 talent you can heal a T1 tower 19,44% per single cast, which is insane. 75s from 1% to full.


R - Overgrowth
AoE BKB piercing Bind (not Root) that issues a stop command. During midgame, you need to identify prime target and save ult to that scenario to obtain best value.

Big value channels (Blackhole, Nightmare)

Particularly if the enemy has BKB


Opponent core that needs to be counter initiated on (AM that jumps your ranged core)

If they have manta or similar dispel you MUST wait until they have popped it.

In this scenario you can use leech seed to root the enemy and if they panic manta you follow up with Overgrowth




When it is of CD you should go play with team always and look for counter initiation

If opponent thinks they are hot shit with their manta, you can Pumpfake the ult to bait them to use manta early.
Even if you have blink, you don’t need to jump next to the opponent, but it is enough to clip the guys with the edges. Use ALT+Rightclick to show radius. Afterwards change that to blink as that is more of a limiter
D -Eyes in the forest
Bonus wards for easily winning the vision game. The biggest difference is that eyes give flying vision and therefore do not need to have line of sight anywhere, this allow you to place them in spots where regular wards would not do anything, and regular dewarding wouldn’t be done.
Most practical example is the ancients in the outer rivers to which you can set vision anywhere on the nearby trees. Regular vision is most often set between the camps and that’s where the dewarding happens. In the end you want to know if enemy core is clearing the camp and their movement is secondary nice to have info.

As a thought exercise you can think:

What vision do I want to set up and where would I place a ward
Where would I put sentry to deward vision here
Where would be eyes in the forest accomplish #1, while being in unlikely spot to be warded



                  
                  Best vision 
                  
                

Eyes in the forest can even see into the Roshan’s pit!


F - Nature’s Guise
Only able to be activated if you have the Treewalking active. Best use is for scenarios where you want to disappear from the map and surprise enemies. Portal to another lane, for example (It is possible to path via the portals without breaking passive, but it’s tough to accomplish)
In your head, try to draw a small circle around all trees, and imagine the rest of the map is lava that you want to avoid.
Fun ways to use:

Capture the wisdom shrine while invisible, which can lead to silly situations if opponents don’t have way to break the tree or get vision
Stay invisible almost standing on the power rune when it is being contested


Talents and skills
Skip leech seed and base damage talents, as you’re not making the most of them. Instead everything boosting the living armor is great
Talent build

Skill build
Most regular skill build. You can vary the first level 3 how you see fit.

Items
Starting items
Brown boots
See “playstyle” -segment for reasoning behind brown boots.
Blood grenade
Buy every game
Wand
Eventually mandatory in every game for the stats and utility + it builds into Holy Locket, which is good upgrade, but not a high priority.
Mana boots
The only real option for support treant. Note that movement speed allows you to cover bigger gaps between trees without breaking nature’s guide.
Shard
Mandatory, as it grants you the eyes of the fore. The only question is, how much do you trust your team to take Tormentor? If uncertain you should buy this right after 15 minutes.
Blink Dagger
Expensive, but insanely good for your positioning and overgrowth usage. It is possible you need to actually buy support items before blink, but depends if your team needs support items desperately. Once obtained use the ALT+Rightclick on blink to draw the blink distance.
Support items
Not really treant specific, so links to general situations under the links

Force Staff
Glimmer Cape
Eul’s Scepter

Playstyle
Earlygame
Movement speed and autoattacks
Brown boots at the start, which increase your movement speed from 280 (308) to 325 (357,5). Numbers in brackets are the values in the trees.
When chasing an enemy, every time you attack you spend 0,6s in the attack animation roughly translating to giving running opponent a (357,5 x 0,6) 214,5 distance. Average hero movement is roughly 300 (see chart below). Formula for chasing and enemy would be:
`214,5 / (357,5 - 300) = 3,73
Few alternative scenarios:
Crystal Maiden
214,5 / (357,5 - 280) = 2,76 [[Marci]] 214,5 / (357,5 - 315) = 5,04
This means you can attack the average enemy roughly every fourth second.
Advantages:

Opponent is caught in the nature’s grasp
Opponent need to path sideways to avoid nature’s grasp
Opponent needs to path around trees (you don’t)

Disadvantages:

You need to leave the treeline

Chart of heroes base movement speed values:



                  
                  Windlace 
                  
                

Windlace stacks with the boots, and if you feel you can bully in the lane, the 225g for 15 (16,5) movement speed might very well be worth the investment.


Laning itself
Use Treewalking to get close to enemy Pos3 and if not possible then Pos4. Typically you hit them twice and then disappear into the trees.
If there is a credible kill potential, you should weave the attacks so that you do the following

Autoattack + Leech seed
Nature’s grasp
Second autoattack
Bloodgrenade and followup autoattacks
Reason for the Spellweaving is that your attack backswing is very long, and you should use the time for nature’s grasp animation to be completed to waste minimal time.



                  
                  Killthreat peak 
                  
                

Assuming your lane can even have killthreat it is from your end reached once you have both Q and W, but will not increase as you’ll be maxing the living armor.




                  
                  Objectives 
                  
                

03:00 Contest the lotus, as Treant is very fine manfighting the other support
06:00 Contest the mid rune,
07:00 From mid walk to the opponents wisdom rune


Midgame
Your function is to provide information to your teammates in the form of eyes in the forest and you being around the map in nature’s guise. When ult is of CD, go join team and use it to Counterinitiate.


                  
                  Shard 
                  
                

Can you get team to do Tormentor at 20min? If not save money right after manaboots to buy shard at 15min mark.


When ult is on CD go push a creepwave if possible with nature’s grasp in order to get your Blink Dagger
Lategame
Your primary concern is landing a good overgrowth. See spell description for how to use it optimally.


                  
                  Nature's grasp +25dmg 
                  
                

Obtained at level 15, you should have the Nature’s grasp maxed out and with this talent you can kill and entire creepwave and push super well


Synergies and advantages

You have advantage with ranged Pos1 that hate being jumped as you are able to easily counter initiate and turn the tide.
Enemy carries that build a BKB are optimal, as the overgrowth can easily waste the BKB to a great extent.
Enemies who jump in and do their damage in few instances struggle against a well placed living armor

Counters

All damage over time effects are terrible for treant, as they are punishing you immediately if you break your Treewalking. Venomancer and Jakiro are matchups that feel frustrating to play against.
Overabundance of dispel is bad as overgrowth is dispellable.
Enemies which have ability to easily deward can actually contest your vision (Zeus, Slark)
Tower pushers that do not leave them halfway for you to heal (Zoo heroes, Death Prophet)
